text:
anya: quick thread on iterator ergonomics + resume token compatibility. two ops incidents last quarter were traced to long-lived client bookmarks breaking after a token-encoding change. we need a safer public surface.

sam: yeah. proposal: make resume blobs opaque and versioned, but keep them small (<1KB). server rotates internal tokens; bookmark contains a stable header with version + HMAC, server can migrate as needed. clients only store the opaque bookmark string.

marie: ergonomics question: should bookmarks be base64 or urlsafe? customers stick tokens into DB keys and urls. urlsafe base64 seems friendlier. also consider a short TTL encoded so stale resumes fail fast.

diego: on the prefetch side — customers want better throughput for small-page scans. server can optionally return a small prefetch_hint JSON: {"avg_items": 120, "window_ms": 1200}. SDK should expose it as a non-authoritative hint that can enable local batching strategies, but must never be required for resume correctness.

anya: agree. and we should explicitly forbid clients from parsing the opaque bookmark. warn in docs. provide a compatibility guarantee: server accepts bookmarks for 18 months after rotation and emits a Deprecation header when using legacy formats. SDKs log a single warning per resume call if header present.

sam: retries + side-effects: paginated list APIs must be idempotent. where that's impossible, the server should require a client-supplied idempotency key. default iterator retry should be safe: retry on network/transient 5xx, but surface a hook to opt into aggressive retry or to disable retries for a given iterator.

marie: cross-language surface ideas (keeps iterator thin):
```py
# Python - idiomatic generator
for page in client.items.list(q):
    for i in page.items:
        process(i)
# resume
book = page.bookmark
client.items.list().resume(book)
```
```ts
// TypeScript - async iterable
for await (const page of client.items.list({q})) {
  page.items.forEach(process)
}
const book = page.bookmark
await client.items.list().resume(book)
```
```go
// Go - explicit iterator
it := client.Items().List(ctx, q)
for it.Next() {
  p := it.Page()
  for _, i := range p.Items { process(i) }
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { return err }
book := it.LastBookmark()
it.Resume(book)
```

diego: transport: we should keep iterator API identical regardless of transport. server advertises supported transports in discovery: paged-JSON over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 framed streaming, or gRPC. SDKs auto-select best transport but allow client config override (transport_preference: ["stream","paged"]). Important: streaming should provide explicit backpressure signals to clients (window frames or a per-iterator token-bucket) so clients don't OOM when prefetch_hint suggests large windows.

anya: good point about memory. default SDK behavior: keep a small in-memory page buffer (configurable) and apply backpressure to the network layer. for languages without native backpressure (e.g., older Go users), expose a MaxBufferedPages option.

sam: how do we surface throttling to app code? if server responds with a graceful throttle (HTTP 429 with Retry-After or a stream-level throttle frame), iterator should surface a RetryAfterError that includes suggested wait. app can catch and either abort or sleep & resume. by default the iterator will wait and retry once.

marie: telemetry: SDK should emit a histogram for resume failures (invalid_bookmark, expired, malformed) and for unexpected live-rewrites (bookmark_migrated). also capture last_request_id from headers on each page and expose it on Page for debugging.

diego: migration plan: new server rollout accepts old bookmarks for 12 months, logs deprecation. we will run a rollout with gradual token format switch and a compatibility-check job that replays persisted bookmarks through a validation endpoint to estimate breakage before cutover.

anya: next steps: draft follow-up RFC covering the bookmark wire format (high-level only), prefetch_hint schema, retry policy knobs, transport capability discovery, and cross-lang iterator examples. assign draft to @marie, review to @sam and @diego.

ops-bot: CI: smoke tests 12/12, integration 7/7, linting 0 warnings :white_check_mark:

sam: tiny nit — add an example for forcing a transport in the client config and a small note about persisted bookmarks in serverless functions where env rotation can be frequent.

anya: noted. thanks all — goal: thin, idiomatic SDK API, no leaked transport/token internals. :rocket:
